channel.title: Darkshield
channel.description: An enterprise integration architect writes about homelabs, self-hosting and AI agents. The wins, the failures, and the 3 AM fixes.

item.title: What AI Got Wrong (And Why That's the Point)
item.description: AI got things wrong on this build more than once. Most of it was a documentation problem, and the rest is why I stay in the loop.

item.title: The Layers: How the Pieces Actually Talk to Each Other
item.description: One front door, one identity decision, simple services and an observer that touches nothing. The shape is what transfers, not the tools.

item.title: Running More Than One AI Without Losing Control
item.description: I split the work between Claude and Gemini, then used branches and reviews to keep two AI contributors from colliding.

item.title: The Delegation Playbook
item.description: One question decides what AI gets to do on my homelab: can this be undone? Everything else follows from it.

item.title: I Built a Little Workshop to Watch My AI Agents Work
item.description: A free, vibe-coded Stark workshop that shows my AI agents handing off work live. No LLM tokens, read-only, and easy to build yourself.

item.title: A Crew of AI Agents Runs My Homelab
item.description: Five AI agents handle the day-to-day running of my servers while I make the decisions. How they fit together, which models do which job, and what went wrong.

item.title: The Document System That Keeps AI Grounded
item.description: One notes file fell apart, so I split the project into numbered topic folders and gave every AI session a file to read first. Click through the layout.

item.title: The Conversation Before the Build: Aligning with AI on Architecture
item.description: Before any config existed I spent my first hours talking architecture with Claude, then wrote it down. Here is the loop and where I keep the leash short.

item.title: Experimenting With Autonomous AI Agents: OpenClaw and Moltbook
item.description: I let an OpenClaw agent loose on Moltbook, a social network for AI agents, and locked it in an LXC on its own VLAN first.

item.title: Building a Resilient Homelab Storage Solution with TrueNAS
item.description: TrueNAS SCALE virtualized on Proxmox at two sites, with local and off-site backups, because redundancy is not a backup.

item.title: Supercharge Your Terminal with OpenCode CLI
item.description: OpenCode is an open-source terminal AI agent that works with cloud models, Groq or local Ollama, so you aren't locked to one vendor.

item.title: Build Your Own Netflix
item.description: A self-hosted request-to-playback pipeline with Ombi, the *Arr apps, qBittorrent, TrueNAS and Jellyfin, so you own your library instead of renting it.

item.title: Building a Homelab
item.description: Why I run a homelab, the three building blocks it rests on, and how to start with old hardware.

item.title: My Personal AI Stack in a Homelab
item.description: The local AI stack I run in my homelab: what each piece does, what plugs into it, and the modest GPU behind it.

item.title: Building Your Own Personal Photo Cloud
item.description: How I replaced paid photo storage with Immich and Nextcloud on two TrueNAS servers that back each other up every night.

item.title: A Site-to-Site WireGuard Tunnel for TrueNAS Replication
item.description: How I joined my home and a friend's house with WireGuard on pfSense so TrueNAS can replicate over SSH without exposing either server.

item.title: Building a Homelab: Technical Expertise at Home
item.description: The goals behind my homelab, the virtualization, VLAN and NAS pieces that make it up, and a five-step way to start your own.
